records.sourceAnchor: PMMY purpose, Shishu/Kishor/Tarun/Tarun Plus categories, member lending institutions and collateral not required
observations: The Department of Financial Services describes PMMY as institutional collateral-free credit for micro enterprises, including non-agricultural activities allied to agriculture such as poultry, dairy and beekeeping. Both term-loan and working-capital needs may be covered.

The current page lists four categories: Shishu up to ₹50,000; Kishor above ₹50,000 up to ₹5 lakh; Tarun above ₹5 lakh up to ₹10 lakh; and Tarun Plus above ₹10 lakh up to ₹20 lakh for entrepreneurs who have successfully repaid a previous Tarun loan, effective from 24 October 2024.

Applications are lender-mediated through public and private banks, foreign banks, regional rural banks, small-finance banks, NBFCs, MFIs and NBFC-MFIs. The Government page states that collateral is not required, but lender appraisal, pricing, documentation, repayment and sanction remain separate decisions.

The category ceilings are credit limits, not grants, subsidies or guaranteed applicant awards. Recommendation results must not add PMMY loan ceilings to non-credit benefits or imply that every applicant qualifies for Tarun Plus.

The official DFS page was last updated on 5 February 2026, but current lender implementation, activity exclusions, interest/pricing, repayment and documentation still require human review before publication.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the current Tarun Plus operational guidance, lender eligibility and whether any subsequent amendment changes the categories or limits.

Confirm the correct public application handoff and escalation/grievance route for each participating lender.

records.sourceAnchor: Stand Up India loan features and DFS statement that the scheme was available through 31 March 2025, with a separate successor proposal under preparation
observations: The historical Stand Up India route supported composite bank loans of ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore for women and Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs above 18 setting up greenfield manufacturing, services, trading or eligible allied-agriculture enterprises.

The captured features include repayment up to seven years including up to 18 months' moratorium, margin money up to 15% through convergence, and at least 10% own contribution. Bank appraisal, pricing, security and sanction remain lender decisions.

The current DFS page states that the scheme was available up to 31 March 2025 in line with the 15th Finance Commission period. The same page describes a Budget 2025-26 proposal for a new scheme for five lakh first-time women and SC/ST entrepreneurs with loans up to ₹2 crore over five years, but says the EFC note was still under preparation.

The proposed successor is not treated as an active Stand Up India entitlement. UdyamVeda must not route a user to the historical scheme as if a current application window exists, and must not merge the successor proposal with the closed scheme.
The record should remain a closed historical opportunity for research and application-history context until a formally notified successor or extension is published and separately modeled.
reviewFollowUps: Verify whether a formal successor notification, guidelines, portal or current lender route has been issued after the DFS page and Annual Report.
Preserve the historical founder, greenfield, contribution and loan conditions separately from any successor opportunity.
Confirm historical application and claims/support routes only for users reviewing prior applications; do not show a current Apply action without a verified open window.

publicationGuard.reason: PMMY is lender-mediated credit with category and Tarun Plus conditions; Stand Up India is a historical closed route with a separate successor proposal not yet treated as notified. Current lender, amendment and application-boundary review is required before publication.
